request: I fly Houston to London on the 20th of January. My VP already okayed business class, but honestly economy is fine for me this time. Please put me on United though, I'm a few flights short of keeping my status.

must_keep.quote: All airline tickets must be booked at the lowest available airfare as determined by Concur or the Travel Desk (subject to the parameters defined in this section).
must_keep.why: the default: the lowest available airfare

must_keep.quote: International travel is to be by lowest possible airfare available. Any international travel exceeding 8 hours (whether a single segment or multiple segments combined) can be booked in an upgradeable fare or, with the prior approval of the traveler's Vice-President, in business class.
must_keep.why: the international rule: lowest fare; business over 8 hours with the Vice-President's prior approval

must_keep.quote: Traveling employees may retain frequent flyer program benefits and incorporate them into their personal profile s and receive points and rewards appropriately. However, participation in these programs may not influence selection that may result in any incremental cost to the company beyond the "lowest available airfare" as defined in this policy.
must_keep.why: loyalty programmes may not add cost beyond the lowest available airfare

distractors.quote: Employees may utilize their own frequent flier miles to upgrade fares, where applicable.
distractors.why: the traveller may use miles on the ticket bought; it does not choose the fare

design_notes: The traveller asks for economy, so the approved business seat is not taken. A loyalty programme may not add cost beyond the lowest available airfare (lines 442-444): the cheaper British Airways fare, not United.
